Publicly Releasable Version DE-FE0032301 Final Report ABSTRACT This project developed and demonstrated a compact, plasma-based natural-gas fuel reformer designed to reduce methane leaks from large-bore natural-gas engines used in pipeline compression and industrial applications. The device converts a fraction of incoming methane to hydrogen and light hydrocarbons, which promote more complete combustion and lower methane slip (see Figure 1). The reformer advanced from conceptual design through bench-scale testing, high-flow validation conducted at Southwest Research Institute’s Metering Research Facility (MRF), and engine-integration testing on two representative engines (AJAX 2802 ULE and Cummins X15N). Measured slip reductions ranged from 1 to 27 percent, depending on engine type and operational configuration, while plasma power consumption remained below one percent of engine output. The project achieved all planned milestones within budget, developed a patentable, low-cost pulse-power electrical system, and established the technical basis for a scalable methane-leak mitigation approach.
